newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek bonds steady in next two months - BofAmerica.
newsitem.headline: Greek bonds steady in next two months - BofAmerica.

text.p: Greek bonds are unlikely to rally in the next two months, the Bank of America said on Tuesday, citing an expected slowdown in disinflation coupled with a looser interpretation of the EMU criteria leaving only Greece out of the single currency in 1999.

"Expectations of a further slowing down in the disinflation process and a new scenario of a more flexible interpretation of the Maastricht criteria, now the most possible scenario (leaving Greece as the only country outside the broader EMU in 1999) make a fresh bond market rally unlikely in the next two months," it said.
Minor bond price corrections from current levels were likely, said Bank of America in its bimonthly bond market strategy report on Italy, Spain and Greece.
Seven-year FRNs and especially the older non-taxable issues offer attractive value in the secondary market at yields of about 70 basis points over T-bills, it said.

The report said there was limited room for further interest rate cuts by the finance ministry in the 12-month T-bill and predicted the rate would ease to 9.4 percent at end-97 from 9.6 percent currently.

"Slowing disinflation and recent signs that further narrowing of currency yield differentials is unsustainable render the Greek ministry of finance reluctant to proceed with further T-bill rate cuts," the report said.

On the ecu/drachma front, Bank of America forecast a two-month period of stabilisation ahead in the 308-311 range with mark/drachma in the tighter 157-158 band. It ruled out a one-time devaluation before entering ERM.
"Recent speculation that the drachma may devalue before entering ERM - so that tensions in the current account deficit be alleviated- seems unfounded," it said."
"A one-time devaluation would hinder the disinflation process and damage the convergence programme's credibility."
Bank America said ecu/drachma rates above the 310.50 level offered good drachma buying opportunities. -- Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
